signal: SIS marked 30 years of ASC innovation by debuting AI-powered SIS Scribe at ASCA 2026 and earned its fourth Best in KLAS award in five years for SIS Charts.

email.body1:
Stephen, saw SIS debuted AI-powered SIS Scribe at ASCA 2026 and earned another Best in KLAS award for SIS Charts.

That recognition and new product usually pull in more ambulatory surgery centers than your team can work before they go quiet. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for SIS off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Stephen, quick follow-up for SIS.

As SIS Scribe and the KLAS win drive interest, most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to convert it, so the coverage gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your region needs to hit target, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Stephen, last bit of proof for SIS.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other healthcare software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Stephen, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority while SIS Scribe rolls out, no problem at all. A product launch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an ASC software motion? I will tailor it to SIS either way.
